FIFO Pick Evidence

Small 3PL warehouses can turn a pick-log CSV into a portable FIFO exception report before a customer audit. Drop in a log and see which picks left an older lot waiting, and which rows are missing or have an ill-formed timestamp — entirely in your browser.

Drag a pick-log CSV here, or

— or paste its contents below —

Don't have one handy? — a small pick log with one deliberate FIFO exception, so you can see the report shape before using your own.

What this is and isn't

  • Everything runs in your browser. The pick log and report are never uploaded — there is no server here to send them to.
  • The CSV needs order_id, sku, lot, received_at, and picked_at columns, with ISO 8601 timestamps that include a timezone.
  • A report is an observation of the supplied rows, not an audit conclusion, compliance determination, or chain-of-custody record. Confirm your warehouse system's own semantics and investigate each observation.
  • Only anonymous, aggregate usage counts (for example "a report was generated") may be recorded locally — never the pick-log contents, order IDs, or SKUs.

This tool vs. a full WMS

A full warehouse-management platform such as Extensiv 3PL Warehouse Manager runs FIFO or lot-order visibility on top of a whole 3PL operation's client, billing, and inventory records. This tool checks one exported pick log instead — no account, no client setup, nothing uploaded. See FIFO Pick Evidence vs. Extensiv for which one answers your question.

Common questions

What counts as a FIFO exception?

A row is flagged when, for the same SKU, an order that arrived earlier was still picked after the order in that row — meaning the newer lot moved out first while older inventory of the same SKU sat waiting. The report names both the row and the older row it was picked ahead of, so you can check the physical pick against the log. See a worked example for the exact rows that do and do not get flagged.

Why does a row show "invalid timestamp" instead of a time?

received_at and picked_at must be ISO 8601 with an explicit timezone, such as a trailing Z or a +00:00 offset. A bare local timestamp with no zone is reported as invalid rather than guessed at, because guessing a timezone would guess the very ordering this report exists to check.

Is my pick log uploaded anywhere?

No. Parsing happens with JavaScript running in your own browser tab. This page makes no network request with your file's contents — there is nothing to intercept because nothing is sent. Only anonymous, aggregate usage counts like "a report was generated" may be recorded locally, with an opt-out below.

Is there a command-line version?

Yes — the same check ships as a local Python CLI (fifo_pick_evidence.py) in this tool's repository, for scheduled runs or CI. See the README for its usage.

← FIFO Pick Evidence

FIFO Pick Evidence vs. Extensiv 3PL Warehouse Manager

Two different shapes: Extensiv 3PL Warehouse Manager runs a 3PL's whole warehouse operation — billing, inventory, receiving, and pick/pack — on one platform. This page is a free, private tool for one question: does a single exported pick log show a FIFO exception, before you raise it with a customer.

What each tool is for

Extensiv 3PL Warehouse Manager (formerly 3PL Central) is a warehouse-management platform built for 3PLs running multiple clients' inventory through one system: client billing, SKU and lot records, receiving, pick/pack workflows, and client-facing reporting all draw on the same underlying data. A FIFO or lot-order view there reflects every transaction the platform has recorded for that client's inventory, and it requires the platform itself, client and SKU setup, and ongoing data entry to produce that view at all. Extensiv's own pricing and current feature set are not repeated here, since this session cannot verify today's figures against Extensiv's current terms; only its well-documented scope as a 3PL warehouse-management platform is described.

This tool does none of what a full WMS does. It has no client records, no SKU database, and no memory between visits. It takes a single pick-log CSV — order_id, sku, lot, received_at, and picked_at columns, already exported or extracted from wherever picks are recorded — and reports, entirely in your browser, which rows picked a newer lot ahead of an older one of the same SKU, and which rows have a missing or ill-formed timestamp. It runs free, needs no account and no client set up in advance, and uploads nothing you type.

QuestionWhere to answer it
I run a 3PL and want FIFO or lot-order visibility generated automatically from the same system that runs billing, receiving, and client-facing reporting for every client.Extensiv 3PL Warehouse Manager — that platform-wide view is what it is built for.
I have one pick log exported as a CSV and want to know if it shows a FIFO exception before a customer audit.This tool — free, instant, private, no account or client setup.
I don't have access to a client's Extensiv instance, or the warehouse doesn't run Extensiv at all.This tool — it needs only the five columns already in the exported log, nothing else in the system.
I need the same FIFO check run continuously across every client and SKU, tied to live receiving and pick transactions.Extensiv 3PL Warehouse Manager — built for the ongoing, platform-wide view, not a single log's before-audit check.
Do I need an account, a configured client, or a SKU database to use the tool?This tool: no. Extensiv's FIFO or lot-order reporting runs inside a configured, ongoing warehouse-management platform.

Most 3PLs get different value from each: Extensiv (or a comparable WMS) for a running, transaction-backed FIFO view across every client and SKU, and a private tool like this one for an instant, no-login check on one exported log before a customer conversation. This page's own report is one log's exception check, not a warehouse system, an audit conclusion, or a substitute for reviewing the physical pick.

This tool needs no account and no sign-in: it is a static page, the check runs in your browser, and once it has loaded it keeps working with the connection off.

Common questions

Should I use this tool or Extensiv 3PL Warehouse Manager?

They solve different problems. Extensiv 3PL Warehouse Manager (formerly 3PL Central) is a full warehouse-management platform built for running a 3PL's whole operation: client billing, inventory records, receiving, pick/pack workflows, and client-facing portals all live in one system, and a FIFO or lot-order report there reflects every transaction the platform has recorded for that client's inventory. It requires the platform, its client and SKU setup, and ongoing data entry to be accurate, and it is built for a 3PL running many clients' inventory through one system of record. This tool does none of that. It takes a single pick-log CSV — order_id, sku, lot, received_at, and picked_at columns already exported or extracted from wherever picks are recorded — and reports, in your browser, which rows picked a newer lot ahead of an older one of the same SKU, and which rows have a missing or ill-formed timestamp. No account, no client setup, and nothing uploaded. A 3PL already running its operation through Extensiv gets FIFO visibility from the platform it already operates in; a warehouse checking one exported log by hand, or without access to a client's Extensiv instance at all, is in the right place here.

what-counts-as-a-fifo-exception.html.text:
← FIFO Pick Evidence

What counts as a FIFO exception?

A row is flagged only when an order that arrived earlier for the same SKU was still picked after it. The table below is the exact fixture the report's own test suite runs to confirm which row gets flagged, which one does not, and why.

Two orders, one SKU, one flagged row

Both rows are SKU A. The earlier-received order (row 2) is picked last, and the later-received order (row 3) is picked first -- so row 3 is flagged, referencing row 2 as the older lot it jumped ahead of.
RowOrderReceivedPickedResult
2OLD-12026-01-012026-01-03no observation
3NEW-12026-01-022026-01-02 12:00fifo-exception — picked before older row 2

Row 2 (OLD-1) arrived first but was not picked until the third of January. Row 3 (NEW-1) arrived a day later and was already picked by noon on the second — before OLD-1 ever left the shelf. NEW-1 is the row flagged, because it is the one that moved out of turn; OLD-1's own line stays clean.

The check runs per SKU: it only compares rows that share the same sku value, so ordinary variation in which SKU gets picked first never produces an observation. A row is also never compared against itself, and a SKU with only one row can never trigger this check regardless of its dates.

Open the checker and load the bundled worked example to see this exact case reported, or drop in your own pick log. Nothing you drop in leaves your browser.

This page explains the check's arithmetic, not warehouse operations or audit standards. It does not replace investigating each observation against your own system's records.

Common questions

What counts as a FIFO exception in a pick log?

A row is flagged when, for the same SKU, an order that arrived earlier was still picked after the order in that row — meaning a newer lot moved out first while older inventory of the same SKU sat waiting. The report names both the flagged row and the older row it was picked ahead of, so the physical pick can be checked against the log.

Does the older row also get flagged, since it was the one left waiting?

No. Only the row that jumped the queue is flagged, with a reference back to the older row it was picked ahead of. The older row's own line in the report stays clean unless it has a problem of its own, such as a missing field.

Does picking two different SKUs out of order ever count as an exception?

No. The comparison only runs within rows sharing the same SKU, so ordinary variation in which SKU gets picked when never produces a fifo-exception observation.
